purpose: Gate E execution/security qualification record for the pre-2.0 artifact. Every row names the executable test that asserts it and the negative case that would catch its removal. This record QUALIFIES author-side coverage; it does NOT discharge the independence requirement, which no author can supply.

components.question: Is the child-process approval surface incapable of self-approval?
components.negativeCase: WorkerApprovalPort throws at construction if a resolve/revoke/invalidate/mutate method appears; recordExecutionOutcome is scoped to the bound workerId.
components.note: Author-side. F8b independence remains a separate release gate (P0-G, separate security track).

components.question: Does a hard policy deny survive every session mode?
components.negativeCase: Deny stays deny across auto/bypass/ask; an allow is never invented; a consumed approval cannot be re-consumed; deny-wins when an allow and a deny both match.
components.note: Structural demonstration. There is no progressive-supervision feature to test, so this is non-bypass of the existing authority, not of a future one.

components.question: Does an approval claimed and then crashed stay consumed rather than silently reusable?
components.negativeCase: A pending claim observed on replay is classified unverified and denied without reissuing authority; a legacy approval with no fingerprint fails closed and is re-asked; silence is never success.
components.note: Covers the crash window between claim and execution, which is the one state where double execution would otherwise be possible.

components.question: Can a worker write outside its declared owned paths?
components.negativeCase: The owned-path rule decides every declared-scope write; a broader capability permission never widens the grant; file.create applies the router backstop to new files as well as overwrites. The bf29449b regression — gate returned the allow before the owned-path rule — is pinned by an explicit allow-listed-capability x session-mode table.
components.note: The parity table (tests/ownership/path-scope.test.ts) is broader than the implementation, per the authorization-parity contract.

components.question: Are denied actions observably denied, and do they leave no side effect?
components.negativeCase: Protected paths are not written; a denied command is classified deny and does not reach dispatch; denial at the port and at dispatch level both produce a deny decision rather than an execution.
components.note: Proven at port and dispatch level. Full TUI operator-denial scenario is NOT exercised — recorded as gap F-03, not claimed.

declaredGaps.gap: No explicit wrong-workspace test for the worker port
declaredGaps.why: The failure mode cannot be constructed through the port (no user-supplied workspace path), but the test itself does not exist

declaredGaps.gap: Tool-level operator denial not exercised through the full TUI scenario
declaredGaps.why: Denial is proven at port and dispatch level only
Prior evidence shows dependency serialization, not rejection of an unsynchronized conflict
Possible timing fragility in an approval test; one unreproduced observation

declaredGaps.gap: D4-04 delegate transport flake bounded, not fixed
declaredGaps.why: 42 consecutive passes, zero reproduction; a delegate case may not be the sole evidence for a baseline

independence.note: Gate E requires qualification 'independently'. Author-side tests cannot supply independence, and an operator waiver records acceptance of author-only testing rather than creating a second party. No independence is claimed.
